name: Unlimited OCR 2

lineage.how_derived: all decoder attention modules replaced by Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention (SR-SWA)

purpose: Parse documents of arbitrary length (dozens to hundreds of pages) in one pass with constant per-step cost: the model looks only at what it transcribes, inspired by human book transcription without re-scanning earlier pages (paper abstract).

license.name: MIT
license.notes: Card tag mit; the HF repo has no LICENSE file, the MIT text was read in the GitHub repo baidu/Unlimited-OCR (Copyright 2026 Baidu).

architecture.kind: vision-language, DeepSeek-V2-style MoE decoder (12 layers, 64 routed + 2 shared experts, 6 active) with SAM-based vision encoder (the README names a SAM attention bias)
architecture.attention: sliding window 128 over generated tokens plus a fixed set of reference tokens (SR-SWA, e.g. 512)
architecture.why_this_design: Card and paper: SR-SWA compresses text-visual attention interactions from ultra-long sequences to a fixed-size set of working references, so per-step decoding latency and memory stay nearly constant regardless of document length; at the hundred-page scale 7.0x per-step speedup over full attention and 5.6x over R-SWA (arXiv abstract).

variants.notes: also Q5_K 2.28, Q6_K 2.74, Q8_0 3.13, BF16 5.88 GB plus mmproj F16 0.83 GB; 15.8k downloads; llama.cpp support of SR-SWA not verified

strengths: constant decode cost over hundreds of pages
multi-page requests keep cross-page context (tables and paragraphs that continue over a page break)
tiny: 6.9 GB BF16, about 3 GB quantized
weaknesses: serving the full long-document mode needs a customized SGLang wheel
no per-language results in the card
best_for: long scanned reports and books to Markdown
soft.maturity: second generation within five months; 604k downloads of the HF repo

tona_fit.reason: MIT, about 3B total and 0.5B active, fits every class; the unbounded-length decoding is exactly what long German reports and contracts need. Quality of v2 on OmniDocBench is not in readable text (v1 93.92 as quoted by another vendor), and German is not evidenced.
blockers: no Tona module for the DeepSeek-OCR-style encoder and the SR-SWA decoder
llama.cpp path does not say whether SR-SWA is implemented
